minutes.headline: Committee approved posting a teacher and aide for a new primary school behavior program; joint workshop with selectmen followed.
minutes.summary: The committee presented the superintendent's award, heard of a proposed small-group program at the primary school for students with social-emotional needs, and voted to proceed with posting the positions. It also signed off on the year-end report and accepted school-supply donations. A resident asked about leftover salary money. The rest was a joint workshop with the Board of Selectmen on Turkey Hill, TC Passios, enrollment, union negotiations, liaisons and joint events.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to proceed with posting a teacher and a paraprofessional for a new small-group behavior program at the primary school.
The committee voted to authorize signing off on the end-of-year financial report and to accept two donations of school supplies.
A resident asked that salary savings from retirements and resignations be returned to the general fund; the business manager said a report is coming.
In a joint workshop, selectmen agreed to give the School Committee the TC Passios conceptual plans so it can comment on needs.
The two boards agreed to try quarterly written updates in place of liaisons, with a check-in in spring.

why_it_matters: The new program adds staff salaries to the school budget, and the cost is not yet known because it depends on where the hires fall on the salary schedule.
The TC Passios plans and the Turkey Hill roof placeholder could become capital requests that residents are later asked to vote on at Town Meeting.
watch_next: More cost information on the new program is promised by the next School Committee meeting.
A report on salary account savings is expected, along with the TC Passios conceptual plans and a spring check-in on quarterly updates.
